_schema: Feature 29 task 29.10 / phase-2 P1.5. Five golden cases on the attachment branches, over the multi-page fixtures in benchmarks/long_doc_fixtures.py. `required` / `forbidden` are prose facts graded by the same checklist judge as benchmarks/agent_eval_golden_facts.json (Gap 479). Every expected figure is DERIVED from the fixture module, never transcribed - regenerate this file with the generator rather than hand-editing a number.
_founder_spot_check: OWED. The fixture figures are authored by the build session, not taken from real documents, and task 29.10's Terra-vs-Luna role decision rests on them.

cases.question: Per this agreement, what interest do we owe on an overdue invoice, and which clause says so?
cases.expected_answer: 1.5% per month, under clause 27.4. The 2.0% in clause 12.1 is a prompt-payment DISCOUNT, not the overdue interest rate.
required: States the overdue interest as 1.5% per month.
forbidden: States the overdue interest as 2.0% (that is clause 12.1's prompt-payment discount).
States that the agreement does not specify an interest rate on overdue amounts.
cases.why_on_file: The rate sits in clause 27.4 of a four-page agreement, with a decoy percentage in clause 12.1 earlier in the document. A model that grabs the first percentage it sees answers 2.0%. This is the long-context recall case.

cases.question: Reconcile this 70-line statement against our records. Which line has no invoice on file?
cases.expected_answer: BRL-201062 (USD 2,788.30) is the line with no invoice on file. It must be named, not counted.
required: Names BRL-201062 as the statement line with no invoice on file.
forbidden: Reports only a count of unmatched lines without naming the reference.
Names a different invoice as the unmatched one.
cases.why_on_file: Line 62 of 70, on the last page. Gap 470's 'name every reference' rule, asked at a length where the model has to actually retain the page.

cases.question: On this 60-line purchase order, is any line priced out of step with the rest? Give the line number and its unit price.
cases.expected_answer: Line 47, at USD 212.75 per unit against a range of 18.40 to 28.40 on every other line.
required: Identifies line 47 as the out-of-step line.
States its unit price as USD 212.75.
forbidden: States that every line is consistently priced.
Identifies a line other than 47 as the outlier.
cases.why_on_file: Requires scanning all 60 lines across three pages and comparing them, not reading a header. The outlier is an order of magnitude above its neighbours.

cases.question: Does this purchase order allow us to ship it in parts?
cases.expected_answer: No. The order states that partial shipments are not permitted. The term is in the footer, after all 55 line items.
required: States that partial shipments are not permitted under this order.
forbidden: States that partial shipments are permitted.
States that the order is silent on partial shipments.
cases.why_on_file: The decisive term is one line at the very end, after 55 rows of line items - the position a model summarising the table will skip.

cases.question: On this delivery note, were all 70 lines delivered in full? Name any line that was short.
cases.expected_answer: No - 3 lines were short by 3 units each: lines 11, 29, 63. All three must be named.
required: States that not all lines were delivered in full.
forbidden: States that every line was delivered in full.
Reports only a count of short lines without naming them.
cases.why_on_file: Three shortfalls scattered across 70 lines and three pages, the last at line 63. Finding one or two of three is the realistic partial-recall failure.
